stem.en: The price of mangoes rises from ₹100 to ₹150 per kg. Nothing else changes. What does the Law of Supply say Seller A will do?

text.en: Offer more kilograms, because each kilogram now brings him more profit.
Offer fewer kilograms, because buyers buy less at a higher price.
Offer the same amount, because the price does not change how many mangoes he has.
Stop selling, and wait until the price goes back to ₹100.

explanation.en: Under the Law of Supply, price and quantity supplied move in the same direction. A higher price brings more profit on each kilogram, so Seller A offers more. Buying less at a higher price is the Law of Demand, which is about buyers, not sellers.

hints.en: This question is about the seller, not the buyers. What does a higher price mean for him?
